sources.citation: OLAC, 'resources in and about the Katua language' (kta), combined catalog as of 2024-12-13 (Internet Archive copy).
sources.note: Catalogue only: lists just Glottolog, Ethnologue, LINGUIST List, and Smith 1973 (oai:sil.org:8311). No grammar, phonology, primary texts or lexicon are archived anywhere in OLAC for kta.

sources.citation: SEAlang: MKS archives keyword/title indexes (vols 1-35), SALA catalogue (sala_main.htm), Mon-Khmer Languages Project classification table and database by-author list.
sources.note: Catalogues only. MKS archive keyword 'Kơtua (1)' = Smith 1973 only; SALA has no Katua/Kotua language page (htm/Kotua.htm and htm/Katua.htm 404) and Kơtua appears only in the Smith 1973 entry; the MKLP classification table lists 'Katua (L) | Ca Tua (LA) kta' under North Bahnaric but its lexical database holds no Katua/Kotua data set.

sources.citation: Ethnologue 19th ed. (2016), 'Katua', Lewis, Simons & Fennig (eds.), Internet Archive copy.
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. Alternate name Ca Tua; population 4,000 (Bradley 2007b); location Kon Tum province, Mang Buk area, west of the Kayong area; 6a Vigorous; part of the Xo Dang official ethnic community. No dialects, no bibliography.

sources.citation: Cheeseman, Nathaniel, Jennifer Herington & Paul Sidwell. 2013. Bahnaric linguistic bibliography with selected annotations. Mon-Khmer Studies 42: xxxiv-lxvii.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; it is a bibliography. Searched the full text for Katua/Kotua/Kơtua/Ca Tua: the only hits are Smith 1973 in the Smith entry list and the line 'Katua 6a kta' in the language index (section 5, p. lxvi). No grammar, phonology, wordlist or Vietnamese-language work on Katua is listed.

sources.citation: Sidwell, Paul. 2009. How many branches in a tree? Cua and East (North) Bahnaric. In Bethwyn Evans (ed.), Discovering history through language: papers in honour of Malcolm Ross, 193-204. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics 605.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Section 3 'Cua and Kơtua' (pp. 196-199) re-uses Smith's 1973 Kơtua forms in Tables 3-4 (nasal hardening, vowel restructuring) and concludes Kơtua 'is found here to be solidly North Bahnaric' (p. 193); fn. 7 notes Diffloth & Zide 1992 relegate Kơtua to 'uncertain' status. No independent Kơtua data and no phonological description.

sources.citation: Smith, Kenneth D. 1973. Eastern North Bahnaric: Cua and Kơtua. Mon-Khmer Studies 4: 113-118.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. The only published Kotua data: c. 40 forms from a 200-word list taken at Mang Buk in Feb. 1969 (informant Nai of Thu Thok village, fn. 4, p. 117). Comparative-historical notes only: final-nasal hardening after non-nasal/non-laryngeal initials, no vowel-register contrast (p. 114), loss of final r, final l > w, voiced fricative z, affricate ts, voiceless lateral fricative hl, prenasalized voiced stops, sometimes prestopped final nasals (p. 116). Disyllabic forms with presyllables occur in the data (apau 'mortar', kaneng 'crossbow', katsek 'bone') but no word-structure or stre…

sources.citation: Any Vietnamese-language documentation of the Ca Tua / Kơ Tua group within the Xơ Đăng nationality (Kon Plông district, Kon Tum), e.g. Institute of Linguistics (Viện Ngôn ngữ học) surveys of Xơ Đăng dialects.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Katua speakers are officially counted as Xơ Đăng; a Vietnamese dialect survey of Xơ Đăng might contain a Ca Tua word list or phonological note. None was found in Cheeseman et al. 2013 or OLAC, so existence is unverified.
